content_html:
Berries last longer when they are kept cold, dry, and free of damaged fruit that can speed deterioration of the rest. There is no need to wash the entire package as soon as you get home; unless you can dry them completely, it is usually better to refrigerate them dry and wash the amount you are about to eat.

Remove soft, leaking, or moldy berries

Damaged berries release moisture and can affect nearby fruit. Check the package when you get home and discard berries with visible mold rather than trimming a small spot from a moldy berry.

Store berries dry with some airflow

Excess condensation encourages deterioration. Keep the container clean, avoid crushing deep layers, and use an absorbent liner if helpful without sealing berries into a wet container.

Wash shortly before eating when practical

Rinse under running water and dry gently. If you prefer prewashing for convenience, remove surface moisture thoroughly before refrigeration because retained water shortens storage life.

Freeze berries you will not use in time

Freeze clean, dry berries in a single layer first so they stay separate, then transfer them to a container. Their texture changes after thawing, but they remain useful for smoothies, sauces, and baking.
